messages:
ian-sdk: heads-up: found a parity bug between Java and Kotlin SDKs around auth refresh + retries that only shows up under the emulator matrix (API 29/30). Java was fine, Kotlin hung.

rachel-java: what was different? same OkHttp version and same interceptor flow?

ian-sdk: same OkHttp 4.x, same token refresh logic conceptually, but Java SDK runs the refresh on a dedicated single-threaded executor (ExecutorService) inside the Authenticator which masks the blocking behavior. Kotlin code used runBlocking on the OkHttp thread and we see dispatcher starvation and stalled calls.

dmitri-platform: can you paste the two approaches?

ian-sdk: Java approach (simplified):
```
// Java SDK
synchronizedTokenRefresher.refreshBlocking(); // runs on executor backed by dedicated threadpool
return newRequestWithToken;
```
Kotlin approach: 
```
runBlocking { tokenRefresher.refresh() } // executed on OkHttp internal thread
return newRequestWithToken
```

ian-sdk: on emulators with limited IO threads the runBlocking path blocks OkHttp internals and you get stuck waiting for connection cleanup. Java executor hedges against that.

rachel-java: interesting that parity hid this. I'd prefer we don't rely on blocking executors long-term. Two options: (1) make Kotlin mimic Java and use a dedicated executor for refresh work inside the Authenticator, or (2) change both SDKs to a non-blocking singleflight coroutine-based refresh that never blocks OkHttp threads.

maya-qa: from a testability perspective (and to avoid regressions), we should add a flaky-emulator harness that simulates concurrent 401s + slow refresh and asserts dispatcher.queuedCalls stays under threshold.

dmitri-platform: agree. I'd favor (2) long-term but (1) is a smaller fix with lower risk. We should also add a doc note for mobile onboarding describing why blocking in interceptors/authenticators is dangerous on Android and recommend the non-blocking pattern.

ian-sdk: implemented a small patch that introduces AuthRefreshExecutor in Kotlin SDK as a short-term parity fix: refreshes are dispatched to a single-threaded executor using executeBlocking, while we work on a coroutine-first rework. Local emulator tests cleared the hang.

rachel-java: can you add a comment in the Java SDK to call out the parity assumption so future changes don't diverge?

ian-sdk: will do. action items I opened: (A) add emulator flaky job token-refresh-parity (API 28-31) to CI, (B) add docs section "Auth refresh: avoid runBlocking in OkHttp callbacks" with example non-blocking pattern, (C) open follow-up to reimplement Kotlin authenticator using singleflight + suspending refresh that never blocks OkHttp threads.

maya-qa: queued flaky job token-refresh-parity (id 15671). I'll run against emulator matrix and report.

dmitri-platform: also add a small SDK metric for okhttp.dispatcher.runningCalls and queuedCalls so we can detect spikes in prod/mobile labs. ops can wire alerts.

ian-sdk: filed PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-kotlin/pull/2107 - includes executor parity patch + test harness + docs stub.

rachel-java: will review and coordinate to add a note to Java repo outlining the expected semantics. Also let's plan the coroutine-first rework in the next sprint.

maya-qa: will validate flaky job results and test PR once CI finishes. If we still see >2% failures under auth-slow scenario we'll block the merge.

ian-sdk: thanks folks. summary: short-term parity via dedicated executor in Kotlin; long-term plan to remove blocking entirely; added emulator test + docs. :thumbsup:
